summary: Persistent 5xx across streaming and poll endpoints during tenant burst leading to runtime GPU eviction and apigw overload
description:
Issue summary:
Customers observed elevated 5xx rates for both long-poll and short-stream endpoints during a concentrated tenant traffic burst. Errors started at ~2026-03-12 08:30 UTC and persisted with periodic waves for ~6 hours. Downstream investigation shows repeated runtime process restarts and kernel-level GPU eviction messages. apigw exhibited queue growth and connection backlog leading to additional upstream resets.

Impact:
- NimbusHealth (dedicated tenant) experienced ~35% request error rate on streaming endpoints and ~20% on poll endpoints for ~6 hours.
- Several in-production features degraded: real-time transcription and message streaming.
- Customer has an active production incident with business impact.

Environment:
- Dedicated deployment for NimbusHealth in prod (us-east-1) on dedicated GPU pool (3x A100 partial partition).
- Model mix: redwood-13b-v1 for heavy completions and redwood-7b-quant for some routing.

Steps to reproduce (observed pattern):
1) Tenant sends high fan-in of mixed short/long streaming sessions (many connections with keepalive ~120s).
2) apigw accept queue and keepalive pool grow; some connections are queued >1s.
3) Serving runtime processes begin to show kernel eviction (nvml/gpu driver messages) and eventually restart.
4) apigw shows 502/503/504 spikes as upstreams become unhealthy or reset.

Observed behavior:
- Repeated runtime exits with logs showing "GPU eviction: kernel preemption" and then restart watchdogs.
- apigw metrics: accept_queue_length spike, per-route 5xx rate up to 40%.
- Autoscaler attempts scale-up but new pods fail with OOM-like driver errors until eviction pressure subsides.

Expected behavior:
- Tenant burst should be absorbed by autoscaler and prefetched KV cache without causing upstream process restarts or kernel-level GPU evictions.

Logs & metrics (examples):
- runtime.log excerpts: "[08:45:12] ERROR gpu_driver: kernel eviction triggered for device 0, nvml:page_fault"; "[08:45:13] INFO watchdog: restarting runtime (exit code 137)"
- apigw metrics: accept_queue_seconds P95 = 1.8s at peak; 5xx-rate per-route = 38%
- node metrics: GPU memory utilization oscillating 60->98% within seconds during long-stream fan-in.
investigation_notes:
Initial hypotheses considered: noisy-tenant GPU fragmentation, driver-level pagefaults triggered by long-pinned KV caches, and streaming keepalive amplification.
Findings to date:
- NVML traces captured frequent MMU page faults on device 0 during the peak.
- Kernel logs on host show driver preemption messages consistent with eviction under heavy migration.
- Prefetch/KV cache warmup coincided with bursts of long-lived streams which pinned memory and prevented efficient scheduler placement.
- Autoscaler added pods but new pods immediately experienced driver pagefaults when routing prefetched tensors due to memory fragmentation.
- apigw backlog amplified retries causing additional load.
Hypothesis: combination of long-lived streaming sessions + large prefetched KV caches for redwood-13b-v1 created transient high GPU memory fragmentation; driver preemption/eviction led to runtime restarts and cascading apigw 5xx.
Next steps planned:
- Coordinate with infra to collect full NVML dumps and host kernel traces for the affected hosts.
- Temporarily throttle prefetch windows for NimbusHealth and cap streaming concurrent sessions as a mitigation.
- Add a short-term scheduler pinning change to avoid packing heavy-prefetch and streaming workloads onto the same GPUs.
workaround: Applied temporary mitigations at 2026-03-13 01:10 UTC: reduced tenant prefetch window by 50% and set a per-tenant concurrent streaming cap to 300 sessions. Observed immediate reduction in runtime restarts and 5xx rate dropped to ~6% within 20 minutes. Note: customer-facing latency slightly increased for cold prefixes.\n
resolution: Mitigation in progress. Short-term cap and prefetch reduction stabilized the fleet. Engineering is implementing a medium-term fix: scheduler change to isolate heavy-prefetch model instances from long-lived streaming workloads and a runtime patch to handle driver pagefault backoff more gracefully. ETA for rollout of scheduler change to staging: 2026-03-18.\n
